name: service-fabric-tools
description: Author, build, package, publish and debug Azure Service Fabric applications (.sfproj) on Windows, macOS and Linux, and explore your clusters.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the Applications and Clusters views, manifest IntelliSense and validation work, but building, restoring, packaging, publishing, removing, building container images and scaffolding are disabled because they run MSBuild, NuGet and the project's PowerShell scripts.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Builds and the project watcher need the files on disk.

serviceFabric.msbuildPath.description: Override path to MSBuild.exe. If empty, the extension auto-detects via vswhere or falls back to 'dotnet msbuild'.

serviceFabric.nugetPath.description: Optional override for the NuGet executable used by 'Service Fabric: Restore NuGet Packages'. Leave empty to auto-detect via Visual Studio Installer or PATH.

serviceFabric.scaffoldAutoRestore.description: When true, automatically run NuGet restore after Create Application / Add Service so the project is immediately buildable. Disable in offline/sandboxed environments.

serviceFabric.scaffold.suppressDevCertPr.description: When true, suppress the post-scaffold prompt to trust the ASP.NET Core HTTPS development certificate after Add New Service. The standalone 'Service Fabric: Trust ASP.NET Core Dev Certificate' command is still available.

serviceFabric.devCert.expirationWarningD.description: Number of days before expiration when 'Service Fabric: Trust ASP.NET Core Dev Certificate' should warn that the cert is expiring soon. Set to 0 to disable expiry warnings.

serviceFabric.debug.suppressInstallPromp.description: When true, skip the pre-flight check that prompts to install the C# extension before attaching to a deployed service. Use in CI / sandboxed environments where the prompt is not desired.

enumDescriptions: Never auto-attach the debugger after Publish. The first successful Publish surfaces a one-time prompt offering to enable this; afterwards the prompt is silenced.
Auto-attach after every successful Publish to a local cluster. Remote-cluster Publishes are unaffected.
serviceFabric.debug.autoAttachOnPublish.description: Whether to automatically attach the debugger after a successful Publish. 'localOnly' only fires when the active cluster is the local dev cluster.

serviceFabric.debug.autoAttachMaxSession.description: Maximum number of debug sessions auto-attach will start in a single Publish. Excess host processes are skipped (the toast reports how many).

serviceFabric.debug.autoAttachReadyTimeo.description: Seconds auto-attach will wait for at least one service replica to reach the Ready state before giving up.

serviceFabric.sdkPath.description: Override path to the Service Fabric SDK installation root (the folder containing Tools\PSModule\ServiceFabricSDK).

serviceFabric.powerShell.executable.description: Which PowerShell host runs the Service Fabric SDK scripts (Windows only). 'auto' uses Windows PowerShell on Windows. On macOS/Linux Publish and Remove use the REST engine instead (see serviceFabric.deploy.engine).

serviceFabric.entra.useAzureCli.markdownDescription: For clusters secured with Microsoft Entra ID, try the Azure CLI's login (`az login`) before signing in through VS Code. Requires the Azure CLI on `PATH`, and your tenant must allow the Azure CLI to request access to the cluster's application.

serviceFabric.entra.clientId.markdownDescription:
Client (application) ID used to sign in to clusters secured with Microsoft Entra ID.

- Empty (default): VS Code's built-in Microsoft sign-in. Your tenant must allow it to request access to the cluster's application.
- `cluster`: the client application registered in the cluster's Entra ID configuration. Its app registration needs `http://localhost` as a mobile and desktop redirect URI.
- Any other value: that application ID, e.g. your own app registration.

serviceFabric.clientCertificates.markdownDescription: Client certificate files for clusters secured with X.509 certificates, keyed by the publish profile's `FindValue` (a thumbprint, or a subject name for `FindBySubjectName`). Values are paths to a `.pfx`/`.p12` or a PEM file with its key; `~` expands to your home folder. Example: `{ "A1B2…": "~/certs/sf-admin.pfx" }`. Used by the REST engine; on Windows the PowerShell engine reads the certificate store. Passphrases are kept in the OS keychain, never in settings.

serviceFabric.confirmDestructiveActions.description: Prompt before Remove / Reset Local Cluster operations.

serviceFabric.diagnostics.showClusterHea.markdownDescription: Show unhealthy applications and services of the active cluster in the **Problems** panel, on the `ApplicationManifest.xml` / `ServiceManifest.xml` they come from. Re-checked every minute while the window is focused.

serviceFabric.clusters.syncSavedClusters.markdownDescription: Sync saved clusters (endpoint, label, security settings and client certificate path) between machines with Settings Sync. Saved clusters are always shared by all workspaces on this machine; client certificate passphrases never sync.

serviceFabric.clusters.autoRefreshSecond.markdownDescription: How often the **Clusters** view re-probes saved clusters and reloads expanded applications, partitions, replicas and nodes, in seconds. Only runs while the view is visible and the window is focused; clusters you disconnected are skipped. `0` turns it off.

serviceFabric.tree.showDeploymentStatus.description: Poll the active cluster to badge applications that are currently deployed.

serviceFabric.diagnostics.enableManifest.description: Enable in-house diagnostics for application/service manifests (parameter usage, version drift, etc.).

serviceFabric.containers.buildBeforePubl.markdownDescription: Before **Publish**, build and push the image of every container service (`docker build` + `docker push`, with `az acr login` for Azure Container Registry images), as **Build and Push Container Images…** does.

serviceFabric.diagnostics.enableSchemaVa.description: Validate Service Fabric XML (application and service manifests, application parameter files) against the Service Fabric schema: unknown elements and attributes, missing required ones, and invalid enumerated values. Completion and hover stay on when this is off.

serviceFabric.deploy.packagePath.description: Override the application package path passed to Deploy-FabricApplication.ps1. Useful when MSBuild outputs the package somewhere other than the project's <OutputPath>/<PackageLocation> and the standard 'pkg\<Configuration>\' location — e.g. monorepo drops to a sibling folder. Accepts an absolute path or a path relative to the .sfproj directory. The resolver looks for ApplicationManifest.xml directly under this path, and (bounded by serviceFabric.deploy.searchMaxDepth) under nested subdirectories. MSBuild property references ($(MSBuildProjectName), $(Configuration), etc.) are expanded against the .sfproj's <PropertyGroup> values. When this setting resolves to a package whose ApplicationTypeName does not match the project's declared type, a modal warning prompts before deploy (not persisted). Leave empty to auto-detect.

serviceFabric.deploy.useMsbuildPropertyE.description: When true, fall back to invoking MSBuild.exe -getProperty: to resolve <OutputPath>/<PackageLocation> values that reference properties defined in imported targets (e.g. Microsoft.ServiceFabric.targets, Directory.Build.props). The in-extension expander handles all properties declared in the .sfproj's own <PropertyGroup> blocks; enable this only when your build relies on imported-property expansion. Adds 1–3 s per Publish on cold cache.

serviceFabric.deploy.suppressMsbuildEval.description: Skip the modal prompt that offers to enable serviceFabric.deploy.useMsbuildPropertyEvaluator when Tier 1 expansion leaves unresolved MSBuild properties (e.g. $(BuildOutputPath) defined in Directory.Build.props). Power users and CI configurations can set this to true to keep Publish behavior strictly governed by useMsbuildPropertyEvaluator. Does not affect projects whose Tier 1 expansion resolves every token.

serviceFabric.deploy.searchMaxDepth.description: Maximum directory depth for the per-candidate ApplicationManifest.xml search applied to each declared package-root candidate (serviceFabric.deploy.packagePath, <PackageLocation>, <OutputPath>, pkg\<Configuration>\, ...). Default 2 covers the depth-0 direct, depth-1 immediate-child, and depth-2 nested-Pkg layouts produced by the SDK templates and common monorepo conventions; increase for deep monorepo drops (e.g. <repo>\artifacts\bin\<App>\<cfg>\sfpkg\<AppType>\). Values outside [1, 16] fall back to the default and emit a warning.

serviceFabric.deploy.promptForApplicatio.description: When true, Publish Application asks which ApplicationParameters\<env>.xml to splat over the publish profile's defaults. When false (default), Publish reads the file paired with the publish profile via its <ApplicationParameterFile Path="..." /> element — so a 5-node publish profile automatically uses the 5-node parameter file. Enable this only when you need to mix-and-match (advanced).

enumDescriptions: Deploy-FabricApplication.ps1 via the Service Fabric SDK (Windows only), as Visual Studio does.
Upload, provision and create/upgrade over the cluster's HTTP gateway. No Service Fabric SDK required.
serviceFabric.deploy.engine.markdownDescription: How Publish / Remove talk to the cluster. `auto` / `rest`: the extension uploads, provisions and creates/upgrades the application over the HTTP gateway; no PowerShell or Service Fabric SDK needed. It requires a cluster whose image store is `fabric:ImageStore` (the default). `powershell`: runs the project's `Deploy-FabricApplication.ps1` through the SDK's PowerShell module, as Visual Studio does (Windows only). Use it for `xstore:` image stores or a customised deploy script; it also needs the cluster's client TCP port (usually 19000) to be reachable.

enumDescriptions: Replace the application only when it is already at the same type and version.
Replace the application whenever it exists and isn't being upgraded.
Never replace an existing application; fail instead.
serviceFabric.deploy.overwriteBehavior.markdownDescription: REST engine only: what Publish does when the application already exists and isn't being upgraded (the `-OverwriteBehavior` of `Publish-NewServiceFabricApplication`). The PowerShell engine keeps the behavior of the project's `Deploy-FabricApplication.ps1`.

enumDescriptions: Never raise versions; publish the manifests as they are.
serviceFabric.deploy.autoBumpVersions.markdownDescription: When Publish upgrades an existing application (publish profile with `<UpgradeDeployment Enabled="true">`, or a saved cluster with `#serviceFabric.deploy.upgradeMode#` on) and the cluster already runs the version being published, or packages changed without a version bump: raise the application type version and the versions of the changed code / config / data packages and their service manifests. Changes are detected against the package published last time to the same cluster; without that record every service is bumped. Versions are written to the source manifests and the built package.

enumDescriptions: Rolling upgrade with health checks; rolls back on failure.
Rolling upgrade that waits for you to move to each upgrade domain.
Don't upgrade: an existing application is replaced according to serviceFabric.deploy.overwriteBehavior.
serviceFabric.deploy.upgradeMode.markdownDescription: How Publish upgrades an existing application when publishing to a saved cluster (no publish profile). Publish profiles use their own `<UpgradeDeployment>` block.

serviceFabric.deploy.copyPackageTimeoutS.markdownDescription: REST engine only: overall time limit, in seconds, for uploading the application package to the image store. The publish profile's `<CopyPackageParameters CopyPackageTimeoutSec>` takes precedence.

serviceFabric.remove.waitSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the cluster to finish tearing down application instances of a type before unregistering it. Remove-ServiceFabricApplication is async — unregistering too soon produces 'Application type and version is still in use'. Set to 0 to skip the wait (and accept the unregister may fail).

serviceFabric.xmlSchemaPath.description: Path to the Service Fabric XSD used for manifest completion, hover and validation. Accepts either a folder containing 'ServiceFabricServiceModel.xsd' or a direct path to the .xsd file. When empty the extension probes the standard SDK install locations (e.g. 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft SDKs\Service Fabric\schemas') and otherwise uses the schema bundled with the extension.

serviceFabric.logLevel.description: Verbosity of the Service Fabric output channel.

serviceFabric.localCluster.endpoint.description: HTTP gateway endpoint of the local development cluster.

enumDescriptions: One-node dev cluster — fastest startup, no failover testing.
Five-node test cluster — supports placement constraints, failover, and rolling upgrades.
serviceFabric.localCluster.nodeCount.description: Default node count for the local Service Fabric dev cluster. Used by 'Start Local Cluster' / 'Reset Local Cluster' when no explicit choice is made.

serviceFabric.telemetry.enabled.description: Opt in to local-only telemetry events (logged to the Service Fabric output channel at debug verbosity). No data leaves the machine. VS Code's global 'telemetry.telemetryLevel' is also honored.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Service Fabric
walkthroughs.description: Open a Service Fabric application, build it, deploy to a local cluster, and attach the debugger.

steps.title: Open a Service Fabric application
steps.description:
Open a folder that contains a `.sfproj` file. The extension activates automatically and the **Service Fabric** view appears in the activity bar.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

steps.title: Start a local development cluster
steps.description:
Run **Service Fabric: Start Local Cluster**. Choose 1-node for fast iteration or 5-node to test failover and placement.
[Start Local Cluster](command:serviceFabric.cluster.startLocal)

steps.title: Build, package, and deploy
steps.description: Right-click the `.sfproj` in the **Applications** view and pick **Package**, then **Publish Application…**. Output streams to the **Service Fabric** output channel.

steps.title: Attach the debugger to a running service
steps.description:
Once your application is deployed, run **Service Fabric: Attach Debugger to Deployed Service…** to pick a code package and start a debug session against the host process.
[Attach Debugger](command:serviceFabric.debug.attachToService)

steps.title: Read the full how-to guide
steps.description:
The bundled how-to guide covers every feature: tree, manifests, build, local cluster, deploy, debug, diagnostics, settings, and troubleshooting.
[Open Help Guide](command:serviceFabric.openHelp)

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_listProjects
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the Service Fabric application projects in this workspace.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the Service Fabric application projects (.sfproj) in the open workspace: application type name and version, application parameters with defaults, service packages (version, manifest path, code packages, endpoints), parameter files and publish profiles. Use it to relate workspace code to what is deployed on a cluster.

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_listClusters
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the saved Service Fabric clusters and their state.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the Service Fabric clusters saved in VS Code: label, HTTP gateway endpoint, local or remote, whether it is the active cluster, connection state (connected/disconnected/unreachable), last known health, node and application counts. Call this first to find a cluster label for the other Service Fabric tools.

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_getClusterHealth
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the health of a Service Fabric cluster.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the aggregated health of a Service Fabric cluster, the descriptions of its unhealthy evaluations (why it is Warning or Error), and the health of each node and application. Read-only.

cluster.description: Label or HTTP gateway endpoint of a saved cluster (see servicefabric_listClusters). Omit to use the active cluster.

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_listApplications
languageModelTools.userDescription: List applications and application types on a Service Fabric cluster.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the applications deployed on a Service Fabric cluster (fabric:/ name, type, version, status, health, application parameters) and the provisioned application types and versions. Read-only.

cluster.description: Label or HTTP gateway endpoint of a saved cluster (see servicefabric_listClusters). Omit to use the active cluster.

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_getApplication
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the services, partitions and replicas of a Service Fabric application.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns one application on a Service Fabric cluster with all of its services (type, stateful/stateless, status, health), their partitions (status, health) and replicas or instances (role, status, health, node). Use it to diagnose unhealthy or failing services. Read-only.

cluster.description: Label or HTTP gateway endpoint of a saved cluster (see servicefabric_listClusters). Omit to use the active cluster.

application.description: Application name, e.g. fabric:/MyApp or MyApp.

languageModelTools.name: servicefabric_getClusterEvents
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get recent events from a Service Fabric cluster's EventStore.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns recent cluster events from the Service Fabric EventStore (node, application, partition, replica and health events), newest first, up to 200. Fails on clusters without EventStore (most local dev clusters). Read-only.

cluster.description: Label or HTTP gateway endpoint of a saved cluster (see servicefabric_listClusters). Omit to use the active cluster.

minutes.description: How far back to look, in minutes (1 to 1440). Default 60.
